title: Finite smooth and locally free filtration of separable point reductions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $k_s/k$ a separable closure, meaning an algebraic separable extension which is separably closed [def-weil-field, def-pc-separably-closed]. Let $Z$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $M$ a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $P\subseteq Z(k_s)$ any set of $k$-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k_s\to Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define recursively $P_1=P$, let $Z_i\hookrightarrow Z$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on the closure of the images of $P_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], let $U_i\subseteq Z_i$ be the union of the opens smooth over $k$ on which $M|_{Z_i}$ is locally free of finite rank [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-module-pullback], and set $P_{i+1}=\{p\in P_i:p\notin U_i\}$. Locally free of finite rank means locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of structure sheaves. Then $Z_i$ is geometrically reduced (its base change to every field extension of $k$ is reduced), $U_i$ is dense in $Z_i$, and on every affine open of $Z_i$ the intersection of the kernels of evaluation at the points of $P_i$ in that affine is zero. Moreover $Z_{i+1}\subseteq Z_i\setminus U_i$, and $P_{t+1}=\varnothing$ for some finite $t\geq0$. Thus $P$ is partitioned by $P_i\setminus P_{i+1}$ for $1\leq i\leq t$. If $P\ne\varnothing$ and $t$ is minimal, a point of $P$ lies in $Z_t$ exactly when it belongs to $P_t$, and all such points lie in $U_t$.

proof.text: First make the construction for an arbitrary subset $Q\subseteq P$, writing $Y$ for its reduced closed closure. The affine description of the reduced induced structure shows that $Y\hookrightarrow Z$ is locally a quotient of rings. On a finite affine cover witnessing finite type over $k$, those quotients are finitely generated $k$-algebras, so $Y$ is of finite type. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), hence $Z$ and $Y$ are Noetherian by the cited finite-type theorem. Every finite-type affine $k$-algebra is finitely presented by the cited Noetherian algebra lemma. Thus $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite presentation. These conclusions apply separately to every $Q=P_i$, including $Q=\varnothing$.

proof.text: On an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Y$, the images of the members of $Q$ landing in $V$ are dense: any nonempty open in $V$ is an open of $Y$ and therefore meets $Q$. Each such morphism factors through $Y$, since its map to a field kills the ideal defining the reduced closure. Let $J$ be the intersection of their evaluation kernels $A\to k_s$. This is a radical ideal and $V(J)$ is the closure of their images, hence all of $V$. Therefore $J=\sqrt{0}=0$, since $Y$ is reduced. This also proves the requested intersection-of-kernels clause for every affine open, without assuming that $Q$ consists of all separable points of $Y$.

proof.text: Let $L/k$ be finite purely inseparable. Choose a $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $L$. The evaluations of Step 2 remain jointly injective on $A\otimes_k L$: if $x=\sum_j a_j\otimes e_j$ has zero image in every $k_s\otimes_k L$, independence of the $e_j$ over $k_s$ gives $p(a_j)=0$ for every $p$ and $j$, so all $a_j=0$. The basis remains a basis after scalar extension, by the coordinate maps $e_j\mapsto\delta_{ij}$. Each target $k_s\otimes_k L$ is reduced by the separably-generated tensor theorem, applied to the reduced $k$-algebra $L$ and the separable algebraic extension $k_s/k$ (empty separating transcendence basis). A nilpotent of $A\otimes_k L$ consequently has zero image in every target and is zero. The finite purely inseparable test now gives reducedness of $A\otimes_k K$ for every extension $K/k$. The affine base-change chart theorem identifies these spectra with an open cover of $Y_K$; hence $Y$ is geometrically reduced. Apply this argument with $Q=P_i$ for each $i$.

source.place: Tags 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness) and 030V (lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension); schemes.tex Tags 01JR and 01I4; finite-basis expansion of BLR 3.3 Lemma 4

proof.text: For $j_i:Z_i\hookrightarrow Z$, put $F_i=j_i^*M$. Since $Z$ is locally Noetherian, coherent $M$ is quasi-coherent of finite type by the cited equivalence. The two pullback lemmas give those same properties for $F_i$. Choose local affine presentations $F_i|_V=\widetilde N$ on $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$; the affine finite-type criterion makes $N$ finitely generated, and $A$ is reduced. Apply reduced-polynomial-module generic freeness with $R=A$, $n=0$, $P=A$, and module $N$. Its dense union of principal opens has $N_f$ free over $A_f$. These free modules have finite bases: finitely many generators use only finitely many basis coordinates, which must contain the whole basis. The tilde localization theorem identifies the restricted sheaf with a finite free structure module on each such principal open. Thus the union $W_i$ of all opens where $F_i$ is locally free of finite rank is dense: every nonempty open meets a local affine chart and then its dense generic-free open. The smooth locus $S_i$ is dense by the geometrically-reduced dense-smooth-open theorem, using Steps 1 and 3. By their definitions $U_i=S_i\cap W_i$: at a point of the intersection, intersect smooth and free neighbourhoods. The intersection of two dense opens is dense, since any nonempty open meets the first in a nonempty open and then meets the second. This proves density of $U_i$.

proof.text: The set of images of $P_{i+1}$ is contained in the closed subset $Z_i\setminus U_i$ of $Z$, so its closure $|Z_{i+1}|$ is contained there. This is also an inclusion of the reduced induced closed subschemes: on affine charts an inclusion of their closed sets reverses the corresponding radical ideals, giving the required quotient map. If $P_i\ne\varnothing$, then $Z_i\ne\varnothing$, and the dense open $U_i$ is nonempty; it follows that $|Z_{i+1}|\subsetneq|Z_i|$. Notice that an arbitrary map into a nonreduced subscheme would not follow merely from image containment; here both structures are the specified reduced induced ones.

source.place: Tag 01J3, affine radical-ideal description; BLR 3.4 Theorem 2 proof, containment of the next closure in the complement

proof.text: If every $P_i$ were nonempty, the nonempty family of closed subsets $\{|Z_i|:i\geq1\}$ of the Noetherian scheme $Z$ would have a minimal member $|Z_j|$ by the cited minimal-element theorem. Step 5 gives the strictly smaller member $|Z_{j+1}|$, a contradiction. Thus $P_{t+1}=\varnothing$ for some finite $t\geq0$. The recursive identity $P_{i+1}=P_i\setminus U_i$ and the nested sets $P_i$ give the disjoint partition by $P_i\setminus P_{i+1}$, by telescoping. For $P=\varnothing$ choose $t=0$, with the empty partition.

source.place: Tag 01OZ, lemma-Noetherian-topology, and topology.tex Tag 0051; BLR 3.4 Theorem 2 proof, termination of the canonical partition

proof.text: Suppose $P\ne\varnothing$ and choose the least such $t$, so $P_t\ne\varnothing$. Every point in $P_t$ lies in $Z_t$ and, since $P_{t+1}=\varnothing$, in $U_t$. Conversely, if $p\in P\setminus P_t$, there is a first index $j<t$ with $p\in P_j\setminus P_{j+1}$, so $p\in U_j$. But $Z_t\subseteq Z_{j+1}\subseteq Z_j\setminus U_j$ by Step 5 and nestedness of the closures. Thus $p$ cannot lie in $Z_t$. This proves both final assertions, also when $t=1$.
